# Otium — hackathon repo

Several people, each with their own coding agent, work in this repo at once. **The hackathon theme is not known yet.** Until a human fills in the Project section below, don't scaffold an app, choose a stack, or add dependencies.

## Project

- **Theme:** TBD
- **Idea:** TBD
- **Stack:** TBD
- **Run:** TBD

## Entire (session tracking)

This repo uses [Entire](https://docs.entire.io). Git hooks attach each agent session to a commit as a **checkpoint** (stored in git refs, synced to `origin` on push). That lets everyone see why code exists and what other agents already tried.

- Install the CLI and run `entire agent add <your-agent>` once per clone. `entire status` should show your agent as enabled. Without this, your sessions won't be recorded.
- For exact commands and flags, run `entire agent-help`; don't guess.
- **Before starting work**, see what others did: `entire checkpoint list`, `entire recap`, and `entire search "<topic>"`.
- **Before changing code you didn't write**, run `entire why <file>:<line>` or `entire checkpoint explain <sha>`.
- Don't commit `.entire/{tmp,metadata,logs}`; they are already gitignored. Don't edit `.claude/settings.json` hooks by hand.

## Coordination rules

1. **Work small and commit often.** Each commit becomes a checkpoint, so many small commits give teammates' agents more context than one big one.
2. **Pull before you start, and rebase before you push** (`git pull --rebase`). Never force-push `main`.
3. **Stay inside your area.** Once the theme is known, list the areas and their owners here. Ask a human before making broad refactors, renaming shared files, or reformatting the whole repo.
4. **Write useful commit messages:** what changed and why, in a single line.
5. **Keep shared decisions in this file.** When a human decides something that affects everyone (stack, folder layout, API contract), add it here in the same commit.
6. **Don't add a dependency** if a few lines of code would do. Never commit secrets; put them in `.env`, which must be gitignored.

## Areas / owners

_TBD once the theme is announced._

content.content:
entire session attach — Attach an existing agent session
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit, or to the commit named by --commit. Use this when hooks failed
to fire or weren't installed when the session started, or to attach a
research session.

How the session is linked follows from two facts about the commit — does it
already have a checkpoint, and is it pushed — the same for HEAD and --commit:
  - It already has a checkpoint: the session is added to it. Git history is
    not changed.
  - It is already pushed: the commit is left unchanged and the link is
    recorded in a new checkpoint, which is pushed right away (under the manual
    checkpoint push policy it waits for 'entire checkpoint push'). The link counts
    once the commit's author attaches it, and names that exact commit: after
    a rebase or amend, attach the session to the new commit.
  - It isn't pushed: the Entire-Checkpoint trailer is added to it, which
    rewrites it and any commits after it on the current branch (their content
    is unchanged). A trailer survives a later rebase. Merges after the commit,
    or a rebase or merge in progress, are refused. If a remote can't be
    reached to confirm the commit isn't pushed, attach refuses rather than
    risk rewriting a shared commit.

attach prints what it is about to do and asks before doing it. Without a
terminal (an agent or a script) it changes nothing and exits non-zero; show
the user what it printed, and once they agree, rerun with --force.

A session can be attached to more than one commit. Each checkpoint records the
turns since the session's previous checkpoint.

# Otium — hackathon repo

Several people, each with their own coding agent, work in this repo at once. **The hackathon theme is not known yet.** Until a human fills in the Project section below, don't scaffold an app, choose a stack, or add dependencies.

## Project

- **Theme:** TBD
- **Idea:** TBD
- **Stack:** TBD
- **Run:** TBD

## Entire (session tracking)

This repo uses [Entire](https://docs.entire.io). Git hooks attach each agent session to a commit as a **checkpoint** (stored in git refs, synced to `origin` on push). That lets everyone see why code exists and what other agents already tried.

- Install the CLI and run `entire agent add <your-agent>` once per clone. `entire status` should show your agent as enabled. Without this, your sessions won't be recorded.
- For exact commands and flags, run `entire agent-help`; don't guess.
- **Before starting work**, see what others did: `entire checkpoint list`, `entire recap`, and `entire search "<topic>"`.
- **Before changing code you didn't write**, run `entire why <file>:<line>` or `entire checkpoint explain <sha>`.
- Don't commit `.entire/{tmp,metadata,logs}`; they are already gitignored. Don't edit `.claude/settings.json` hooks by hand.

## Coordination rules

1. **Work small and commit often.** Each commit becomes a checkpoint, so many small commits give teammates' agents more context than one big one.
2. **Pull before you start, and rebase before you push** (`git pull --rebase`). Never force-push `main`.
3. **Stay inside your area.** Once the theme is known, list the areas and their owners here. Ask a human before making broad refactors, renaming shared files, or reformatting the whole repo.
4. **Write useful commit messages:** what changed and why, in a single line.
5. **Keep shared decisions in this file.** When a human decides something that affects everyone (stack, folder layout, API contract), add it here in the same commit.
6. **Don't add a dependency** if a few lines of code would do. Never commit secrets; put them in `.env`, which must be gitignored.

## Areas / owners

_TBD once the theme is announced._

content.text:
I pushed to `origin/main`, and the first checkpoint went up with it. Teammates on macOS need to do this once each:

```sh
# 1. Install the Entire CLI (Homebrew)
brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire
entire version

# 2. Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/atisDu/Otium.git && cd Otium

# 3. Turn on recording for your agent (the important step)
entire enable --agent claude-code      # or: codex, cursor, opencode, copilot-cli
ls .git/hooks/post-commit              # this file must exist

# 4. Check what's been done so far
entire checkpoint list
```

**Step 3 is easy to miss.** Git hooks aren't copied when you clone. I tested a fresh clone: it had no hooks, yet `entire status` still said "Enabled". Anyone who skips step 3 gets no checkpoints for their commits, and nothing warns them.

My first `CLAUDE.md` gave the wrong setup command (`entire agent add`) and said `entire status` was a valid check. I fixed both and pushed the fix as a second commit.

**If someone commits from a GUI app** such as GitHub Desktop, add `--absolute-git-hook-path` to step 3. Otherwise the hooks may not find `entire`, because GUI apps don't load the shell settings that put it on the PATH.

**Not checked:**
- Whether `entire enable` asks for `entire login`. The docs only mention login for hosted and mirror features.
- That `enable` leaves the shared `.entire/settings.json` alone. The help text suggests it only rewrites that file when you pass `--project`, but I didn't run it on a clone to confirm.

The second commit doesn't have a checkpoint yet. That's expected: this session started before the repo had any commits, so Entire wasn't tracking it until now. Your next commit should pick it up.

message.content: Ok, whats the best way for the agents to collaborate and not create merge conflicts? Branches or something other?

content.text:
I'd use short-lived branches, one per task, merged into `main` within about an hour. Agents produce a lot of code quickly, so a branch left open for half a day ends in a large merge conflict. Conflicts come from long-lived branches and shared files, not from branches themselves.

**What prevents conflicts:**

1. **One person builds the skeleton first.** When the theme drops, one agent creates the folder layout, the dependency files (`package.json` or similar), the router or entry point, and the shared types or API contract, then pushes. Everyone else starts after that. Most hackathon conflicts happen in those few shared files.
2. **Each person owns a directory.** Record it in the "Areas / owners" section of `CLAUDE.md`, e.g. `frontend/` for Ana and `api/` for Ben. An agent that stays in its own directory rarely conflicts with anyone.
3. **Shared files get small edits only.** Adding a route or a dependency should be its own small commit, pushed right away and not bundled with feature work.
4. **Keep branches short:** `git pull --rebase` before starting, merge to `main` as soon as something works, and delete the branch. Skip PR reviews; there's no time at a hackathon. Use a PR only when it touches another person's area.
5. **Agree on interfaces before building.** Write the API shapes or data types into `CLAUDE.md` first. Then frontend and backend agents can work in parallel against the same contract without editing each other's files.
6. **Run several agents in separate worktrees.** If one person runs more than one agent, give each its own git worktree (`git worktree add ../otium-ui ui-branch`). Two agents in one folder will overwrite each other's files.

Entire records checkpoints on any branch and they survive rebases, so this setup doesn't cost you any history.

If a conflict happens anyway, have an agent resolve it. It can run `entire why` on the conflicting lines to see what each side was trying to do.

## Entire (session tracking)

This repo uses [Entire](https://docs.entire.io). Git hooks attach each agent session to a commit as a **checkpoint** (stored in git refs, synced to `origin` on push). That lets everyone see why code exists and what other agents already tried.


### Environment variables (`.env`, names owned by A)

```text
CALA_API_KEY=
CALA_BASE_URL=https://api.cala.ai/v1

GEMINI_MODEL_FAST=          # Flash-tier model id
```

## 4. Cala — what we know (tested 13 Nov)

- REST base `https://api.cala.ai/v1`, header `X-API-KEY: <key>`, `Content-Type: application/json`. Keys at console.cala.ai/api-keys; hackathon credits with promo code `MAKEUNICORNSREAL` (Billing → Extra credits).
  Exact query params/paths for the entity endpoints: **verify at docs.cala.ai/api-reference** before coding.
- `POST /knowledge/query` `{"input": "..."}` → structured rows + `entities[]` (IDs). Natural language or dot-notation: `companies.industry=X.country=Finland.funding_stage=Seed OR Series A.return(name, description, funding_stage, total_funding).limit=15`. Numbers come back as approximate strings ("~€15M", "over $100M").
- `POST /knowledge/search` `{"input": "..."}` → markdown answer + `explainability[]` (claim → reference IDs) + `context[]` (reference ID → source URL). Best source for "who led which round".
- Entity search by name (fuzzy, filter by entity type), entity lookup by LEI/CIK/etc., entity retrieval by UUID with a projection body `{"properties": [...], "relationships": {"outgoing": {"REL": {"limit": N}}, "incoming": {...}}}`, entity introspection (which fields/relationships exist for that entity).
- **Company** relationships: outgoing `OPERATES_IN_INDUSTRY`, `PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND` (role `ISSUER`), `HAS_DOMAIN_NAME`; incoming `INVESTED_IN`, `IS_BOARD_MEMBER_OF`, `FOUNDED`, `IS_CEO_OF`, `WORKS_AT`. Properties incl. `funding_stage`, `total_funding`, `founding_date`, `headquarters_address`, `description`.
- **Investor** (Organization) relationships: outgoing `INVESTED_IN` (portfolio, sourced, **no dates**), `PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND` (role `INVESTOR`, sometimes `is_lead: true` — sparse).
- **FundingRound** properties: `round_label`, `announcement_date`, `transaction_value`, `transaction_value_units`, `instrument`.
- Every property/relationship carries `sources[]` with `name`, `document` (URL), `date`, `source_rank` (`PRIMARY` | `FILING` | `PRESS` | `AGGREGATOR`; may be missing → `UNKNOWN`).
- Industry tags are coarse (all defence → `AEROSPACE_AND_DEFENSE`) → competitors need vector search + LLM judging.
- Known mismatch: "Inflection" (VC) resolved to Inflection AI → always check type + description for investors.

Demo data: Kelluu (Series A, led by NATO Innovation Fund; also Keen Venture Partners, Gungnir Capital, Tesi). Maki.vc leads defence pre-seeds (Aavuus, Metaktik). Counter-drone set for a conflict demo: Sensofusion, Stendr, Nordic Air Defence.

---

## 5. Contracts (summary of `contracts/`; the files win if they differ)

### 5.1 Models — `contracts/schemas.py`

```python
from typing import Literal, Protocol
from pydantic import BaseModel

CONTRACT_VERSION = "1.0.0"

SourceRank = Literal["PRIMARY", "FILING", "PRESS", "AGGREGATOR", "UNKNOWN"]

class Source(BaseModel):
    name: str
    url: str | None = None
    date: str | None = None          # ISO date or partial ("2025-10")
    rank: SourceRank = "UNKNOWN"

class EntityRef(BaseModel):
    id: str                          # Cala UUID
    name: str
    type: str                        # Company | Organization | Person | FundingRound ...
    description: str | None = None

class Company(EntityRef):
    industries: list[str] = []
    stage: str | None = None
    country: str | None = None
    total_funding_text: str | None = None
    sources: list[Source] = []

class RoundInvestor(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    is_lead: bool | None = None      # None = unknown

class Round(BaseModel):
    id: str
    company_id: str
    label: str | None = None         # "Seed", "Series A" ...
    date: str | None = None
    amount_text: str | None = None
    amount_eur: float | None = None
    investors: list[RoundInvestor] = []
    sources: list[Source] = []

class PortfolioLink(BaseModel):
    investor_id: str
    company: EntityRef
    sources: list[Source] = []

class PersonLink(BaseModel):
    person: EntityRef
    company_id: str
    role: Literal["BOARD", "FOUNDER", "CEO", "EMPLOYEE"]
    sources: list[Source] = []

class Competitor(BaseModel):
    company: Company
    reason: str
    similarity: float | None = None

class Conflict(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["PORTFOLIO", "BOARD"]
    competitor: EntityRef
    via_person: EntityRef | None = None
    sources: list[Source] = []

class Reason(BaseModel):
    text: str
    sources: list[Source] = []

class InvestorScore(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    score: float
    conflict: Conflict | None = None
    leads_in_space: int = 0
    rounds_in_space: int = 0
    last_lead_date: str | None = None
    warm_paths: list[Reason] = []
    reasons: list[Reason] = []

class FounderReport(BaseModel):
    company: Company
    competitors: list[Competitor]
    pitch: list[InvestorScore]
    skip: list[InvestorScore]

class InvestorCheck(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    company: Company
    conflicts: list[Conflict]
    competitors: list[Competitor]
    rounds: list[Round]

class Brief(BaseModel):
    investor_id: str
    company_id: str
    markdown: str
    citations: list[Source]

class AgentEvent(BaseModel):          # streamed by /api/jobs/{id}/stream and /api/chat
    type: Literal["step", "brief", "error", "done"]
    message: str | None = None
    brief: Brief | None = None
```

### 5.2 Data layer interface — A implements, B consumes

```python
class DataStore(Protocol):
    async def resolve(self, name: str, kind: Literal["company", "investor"]) -> list[EntityRef]: ...
    async def company(self, id: str) -> Company: ...
    async def rounds(self, company_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
    async def investor_rounds(self, investor_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
    async def portfolio(self, investor_id: str) -> list[PortfolioLink]: ...
    async def people(self, company_id: str) -> list[PersonLink]: ...
    async def candidate_competitors(self, company: Company, k: int = 30) -> list[Company]: ...
    async def co_investors(self, investor_id: str) -> list[tuple[EntityRef, int]]: ...
    async def sourced_answer(self, question: str) -> tuple[str, list[Reason]]: ...  # knowledge_search
```

`backend/data/__init__.py` exposes `get_store() -> DataStore`, returning `FakeDataStore` when `USE_FAKE_STORE=true`, else the real store. B only ever calls `get_store()`.

### 5.3 REST API — B implements, C consumes

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/resolve` | `{name, kind}` | `EntityRef[]` |
| POST | `/api/founder/analyze` | `{company_id}` | `FounderReport` |
| POST | `/api/investor/check` | `{investor_id, company_id}` | `InvestorCheck` |
| POST | `/api/brief` | `{investor_id, company_id}` | `Brief` |
| POST | `/api/slush-prep` | `{company_id, investor_names: string[]}` | `{job_id}` |
| GET | `/api/jobs/{id}/stream` | — | SSE stream of `AgentEvent` |
| POST | `/api/chat` | `{company_id?, investor_id?, message}` | SSE stream of `AgentEvent` (type `step` = text chunks) |
| GET | `/api/health` | — | `{ok: true, contract_version}` |

Errors: HTTP 4xx/5xx with `{error: string}`. CORS open for the frontend origin.

### 5.4 MCP tools — B implements (thin wrappers over core)

`resolve_company`, `find_competitors`, `get_rounds`, `investor_profile`, `check_conflict`, `rank_investors`, `investor_brief`. Inputs are entity IDs (plus `name` for `resolve_company`); outputs are the contract models as JSON.

### 5.5 Fixtures — `contracts/fixtures/`

- `raw/` — raw Cala responses (A records them; never hand-edited).
- `models/` — contract-model JSON built from raw (`company_<id>.json`, `rounds_<company_id>.json`, `portfolio_<investor_id>.json`, `founder_report_<company_id>.json`, ...).
- `FakeDataStore` reads `models/`. C's mock API serves `models/founder_report_*.json` etc.

---

## 6. Role briefs

### Agent A — Data & infra

You own the **only** code that talks to Cala, Atlas and Verda. Everything you return is a contract model with sources attached.

- `cala_client.py`: async httpx client, `X-API-KEY`, retries with backoff, concurrency limit (semaphore, start at 8), timeout, log every call (endpoint, ms, cache hit) for credit tracking.
- `store.py`: `CalaDataStore` implementing `DataStore`. Map Cala JSON → models in small, tested mapper functions (one per model). Use introspection results to request only existing fields.
- `parsers.py`: amount text → EUR float (handle ~, over, M/B/K, $ / € / £ with a fixed FX table), partial dates → ISO prefix. Unparseable → `None`, never raise.
- Investor resolution: filter to Organization/Company types; prefer descriptions mentioning venture/capital/fund/invest.
- `cache/atlas.py`: wrap every Cala call — key = endpoint + entity ID or hash of input; TTL 24 h; `CACHE_ONLY=true` mode for the demo (no network).
- `cache/vector.py`: embed `name + description`; Atlas Vector Search index; `candidate_competitors` = top-k vector neighbours ∪ `knowledge_query` on same industry + Nordic/Baltic countries + adjacent stages; dedupe by ID; exclude the company itself.
- `batch/precompute_graph.py`: Verda batch job — list active Nordic/Baltic investors, fetch portfolios and rounds, write `investor_graph` (co-investor counts), `investor_activity` (last lead, rounds per sector/stage) and embeddings to Atlas. Idempotent, resumable, logs progress.
- `deploy/`: Dockerfile for the backend (API + MCP server), run instructions for a Verda CPU instance in `deploy/verda.md`.

### Agent B — Intelligence

You own the logic. Develop on `FakeDataStore` (`USE_FAKE_STORE=true`); never call Cala directly — always `get_store()`.

- `core/competitors.py`: `find_competitors(company) -> list[Competitor]`. Get candidates from the store, ask Gemini (fast model, structured JSON output, temperature 0) to keep 10–15 direct competitors with a one-line reason each. Output may only contain candidate IDs (reject anything else).
- `core/conflict.py`: `check_conflict(investor_id, competitors) -> list[Conflict]`. PORTFOLIO = `portfolio(investor)` ∩ competitor IDs. BOARD = people of each competitor with role BOARD who are linked to the investor. Sources = union of the edges used.
- `core/scoring.py`: `rank_investors(company) -> FounderReport`. Investors = everyone in competitors' rounds. Signals: `leads_in_space`, `rounds_in_space`, recency of last lead, warm paths (`co_investors` overlap with the company's current investors). Any conflict → `skip`. Weights in one dict at the top of the file. Every number in `reasons` has sources.
- `core/briefs.py`: `investor_brief(investor_id, company_id) -> Brief`. Facts from store + `sourced_answer()`; Gemini only formats into one page; every sentence must map to a citation.
- `agent/`: Gemini function-calling loop over `tools.py` (core functions + `sourced_answer`). Max 12 tool calls per job, emits `AgentEvent`s. Powers slush-prep and chat.
- `mcp_server/server.py`: MCP tools from §5.4.
- `api/main.py`: routes exactly per §5.3, responses validated by the models, CORS, `/api/health`.
- Tests: `backend/tests/core/` with an eval set of known cases (TODO B8).

### Agent C — Product

You own what people see. Develop against `frontend/mock/` (fixture-based, same shapes as §5.3); switch to the real backend by setting `API_URL`.

- TypeScript types in `frontend/lib/types.ts` mirror `contracts/schemas.py` exactly (same field names).
- One API client module `frontend/lib/api.ts`; components never call `fetch` directly.
- Screens: Home (mode toggle + entity resolve/confirm), Founder report (competitor chips, Pitch list, Skip list with conflict reason first), Investor brief, Investor check, Slush prep (paste list → live agent steps → brief cards), Chat panel.
- Every claim shows a **source badge**: rank (Primary / Filing / Press / Aggregator), date, link.
- States: loading, empty, error for every screen. Fast, clean, no clutter.
- `docs/` + `README.md`: setup, architecture, how Cala/Gemini/Atlas/Verda are used, demo script, pitch notes. Verda's judges require the process to be documented.

## 4. Cala — what we know (tested 13 Nov)

- REST base `https://api.cala.ai/v1`, header `X-API-KEY: <key>`, `Content-Type: application/json`. Keys at console.cala.ai/api-keys; hackathon credits with promo code `MAKEUNICORNSREAL` (Billing → Extra credits).
  Exact query params/paths for the entity endpoints: **verify at docs.cala.ai/api-reference** before coding.
- `POST /knowledge/query` `{"input": "..."}` → structured rows + `entities[]` (IDs). Natural language or dot-notation: `companies.industry=X.country=Finland.funding_stage=Seed OR Series A.return(name, description, funding_stage, total_funding).limit=15`. Numbers come back as approximate strings ("~€15M", "over $100M").
- `POST /knowledge/search` `{"input": "..."}` → markdown answer + `explainability[]` (claim → reference IDs) + `context[]` (reference ID → source URL). Best source for "who led which round".
- Entity search by name (fuzzy, filter by entity type), entity lookup by LEI/CIK/etc., entity retrieval by UUID with a projection body `{"properties": [...], "relationships": {"outgoing": {"REL": {"limit": N}}, "incoming": {...}}}`, entity introspection (which fields/relationships exist for that entity).
- **Company** relationships: outgoing `OPERATES_IN_INDUSTRY`, `PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND` (role `ISSUER`), `HAS_DOMAIN_NAME`; incoming `INVESTED_IN`, `IS_BOARD_MEMBER_OF`, `FOUNDED`, `IS_CEO_OF`, `WORKS_AT`. Properties incl. `funding_stage`, `total_funding`, `founding_date`, `headquarters_address`, `description`.
- **Investor** (Organization) relationships: outgoing `INVESTED_IN` (portfolio, sourced, **no dates**), `PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND` (role `INVESTOR`, sometimes `is_lead: true` — sparse).
- **FundingRound** properties: `round_label`, `announcement_date`, `transaction_value`, `transaction_value_units`, `instrument`.
- Every property/relationship carries `sources[]` with `name`, `document` (URL), `date`, `source_rank` (`PRIMARY` | `FILING` | `PRESS` | `AGGREGATOR`; may be missing → `UNKNOWN`).
- Industry tags are coarse (all defence → `AEROSPACE_AND_DEFENSE`) → competitors need vector search + LLM judging.
- Known mismatch: "Inflection" (VC) resolved to Inflection AI → always check type + description for investors.

Demo data: Kelluu (Series A, led by NATO Innovation Fund; also Keen Venture Partners, Gungnir Capital, Tesi). Maki.vc leads defence pre-seeds (Aavuus, Metaktik). Counter-drone set for a conflict demo: Sensofusion, Stendr, Nordic Air Defence.

## 5. Contracts (summary of `contracts/`; the files win if they differ)

### 5.1 Models — `contracts/schemas.py`

```python
from typing import Literal, Protocol
from pydantic import BaseModel

CONTRACT_VERSION = "1.0.0"

SourceRank = Literal["PRIMARY", "FILING", "PRESS", "AGGREGATOR", "UNKNOWN"]

class Source(BaseModel):
    name: str
    url: str | None = None
    date: str | None = None          # ISO date or partial ("2025-10")
    rank: SourceRank = "UNKNOWN"

class EntityRef(BaseModel):
    id: str                          # Cala UUID
    name: str
    type: str                        # Company | Organization | Person | FundingRound ...
    description: str | None = None

class Company(EntityRef):
    industries: list[str] = []
    stage: str | None = None
    country: str | None = None
    total_funding_text: str | None = None
    sources: list[Source] = []

class RoundInvestor(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    is_lead: bool | None = None      # None = unknown

class Round(BaseModel):
    id: str
    company_id: str
    label: str | None = None         # "Seed", "Series A" ...
    date: str | None = None
    amount_text: str | None = None
    amount_eur: float | None = None
    investors: list[RoundInvestor] = []
    sources: list[Source] = []

class PortfolioLink(BaseModel):
    investor_id: str
    company: EntityRef
    sources: list[Source] = []

class PersonLink(BaseModel):
    person: EntityRef
    company_id: str
    role: Literal["BOARD", "FOUNDER", "CEO", "EMPLOYEE"]
    sources: list[Source] = []

class Competitor(BaseModel):
    company: Company
    reason: str
    similarity: float | None = None

class Conflict(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["PORTFOLIO", "BOARD"]
    competitor: EntityRef
    via_person: EntityRef | None = None
    sources: list[Source] = []

class Reason(BaseModel):
    text: str
    sources: list[Source] = []

class InvestorScore(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    score: float
    conflict: Conflict | None = None
    leads_in_space: int = 0
    rounds_in_space: int = 0
    last_lead_date: str | None = None
    warm_paths: list[Reason] = []
    reasons: list[Reason] = []

class FounderReport(BaseModel):
    company: Company
    competitors: list[Competitor]
    pitch: list[InvestorScore]
    skip: list[InvestorScore]

class InvestorCheck(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    company: Company
    conflicts: list[Conflict]
    competitors: list[Competitor]
    rounds: list[Round]

class Brief(BaseModel):
    investor_id: str
    company_id: str
    markdown: str
    citations: list[Source]

class AgentEvent(BaseModel):          # streamed by /api/jobs/{id}/stream and /api/chat
    type: Literal["step", "brief", "error", "done"]
    message: str | None = None
    brief: Brief | None = None
```

### 5.2 Data layer interface — A implements, B consumes

```python
class DataStore(Protocol):
    async def resolve(self, name: str, kind: Literal["company", "investor"]) -> list[EntityRef]: ...
    async def company(self, id: str) -> Company: ...
    async def rounds(self, company_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
    async def investor_rounds(self, investor_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
    async def portfolio(self, investor_id: str) -> list[PortfolioLink]: ...
    async def people(self, company_id: str) -> list[PersonLink]: ...
    async def candidate_competitors(self, company: Company, k: int = 30) -> list[Company]: ...
    async def co_investors(self, investor_id: str) -> list[tuple[EntityRef, int]]: ...
    async def sourced_answer(self, question: str) -> tuple[str, list[Reason]]: ...  # knowledge_search
```

`backend/data/__init__.py` exposes `get_store() -> DataStore`, returning `FakeDataStore` when `USE_FAKE_STORE=true`, else the real store. B only ever calls `get_store()`.

## 6. Role briefs

### Agent A — Data & infra

You own the **only** code that talks to Cala, Atlas and Verda. Everything you return is a contract model with sources attached.

- `cala_client.py`: async httpx client, `X-API-KEY`, retries with backoff, concurrency limit (semaphore, start at 8), timeout, log every call (endpoint, ms, cache hit) for credit tracking.
- `store.py`: `CalaDataStore` implementing `DataStore`. Map Cala JSON → models in small, tested mapper functions (one per model). Use introspection results to request only existing fields.
- `parsers.py`: amount text → EUR float (handle ~, over, M/B/K, $ / € / £ with a fixed FX table), partial dates → ISO prefix. Unparseable → `None`, never raise.
- Investor resolution: filter to Organization/Company types; prefer descriptions mentioning venture/capital/fund/invest.
- `cache/atlas.py`: wrap every Cala call — key = endpoint + entity ID or hash of input; TTL 24 h; `CACHE_ONLY=true` mode for the demo (no network).
- `cache/vector.py`: embed `name + description`; Atlas Vector Search index; `candidate_competitors` = top-k vector neighbours ∪ `knowledge_query` on same industry + Nordic/Baltic countries + adjacent stages; dedupe by ID; exclude the company itself.
- `batch/precompute_graph.py`: Verda batch job — list active Nordic/Baltic investors, fetch portfolios and rounds, write `investor_graph` (co-investor counts), `investor_activity` (last lead, rounds per sector/stage) and embeddings to Atlas. Idempotent, resumable, logs progress.
- `deploy/`: Dockerfile for the backend (API + MCP server), run instructions for a Verda CPU instance in `deploy/verda.md`.

### Agent B — Intelligence

You own the logic. Develop on `FakeDataStore` (`USE_FAKE_STORE=true`); never call Cala directly — always `get_store()`.

- `core/competitors.py`: `find_competitors(company) -> list[Competitor]`. Get candidates from the store, ask Gemini (fast model, structured JSON output, temperature 0) to keep 10–15 direct competitors with a one-line reason each. Output may only contain candidate IDs (reject anything else).
- `core/conflict.py`: `check_conflict(investor_id, competitors) -> list[Conflict]`. PORTFOLIO = `portfolio(investor)` ∩ competitor IDs. BOARD = people of each competitor with role BOARD who are linked to the investor. Sources = union of the edges used.
- `core/scoring.py`: `rank_investors(company) -> FounderReport`. Investors = everyone in competitors' rounds. Signals: `leads_in_space`, `rounds_in_space`, recency of last lead, warm paths (`co_investors` overlap with the company's current investors). Any conflict → `skip`. Weights in one dict at the top of the file. Every number in `reasons` has sources.
- `core/briefs.py`: `investor_brief(investor_id, company_id) -> Brief`. Facts from store + `sourced_answer()`; Gemini only formats into one page; every sentence must map to a citation.
- `agent/`: Gemini function-calling loop over `tools.py` (core functions + `sourced_answer`). Max 12 tool calls per job, emits `AgentEvent`s. Powers slush-prep and chat.
- `mcp_server/server.py`: MCP tools from §5.4.
- `api/main.py`: routes exactly per §5.3, responses validated by the models, CORS, `/api/health`.
- Tests: `backend/tests/core/` with an eval set of known cases (TODO B8).

### Agent C — Product

You own what people see. Develop against `frontend/mock/` (fixture-based, same shapes as §5.3); switch to the real backend by setting `API_URL`.

- TypeScript types in `frontend/lib/types.ts` mirror `contracts/schemas.py` exactly (same field names).
- One API client module `frontend/lib/api.ts`; components never call `fetch` directly.
- Screens: Home (mode toggle + entity resolve/confirm), Founder report (competitor chips, Pitch list, Skip list with conflict reason first), Investor brief, Investor check, Slush prep (paste list → live agent steps → brief cards), Chat panel.
- Every claim shows a **source badge**: rank (Primary / Filing / Press / Aggregator), date, link.
- States: loading, empty, error for every screen. Fast, clean, no clutter.
- `docs/` + `README.md`: setup, architecture, how Cala/Gemini/Atlas/Verda are used, demo script, pitch notes. Verda's judges require the process to be documented.

# Pitchlist — Project Overview

Nov 13, 2026 · @Atis Dubrovskis

## The idea

**Pitchlist tells you who's a fit and who has a conflict, from either side of the table.** It's a web app plus an MCP server, built on Cala's connected, sourced data on companies, funding rounds and investors.

**The problem.** Founders build investor lists from logo walls and gut feeling, then waste weeks on three kinds of investor who were never going to say yes:

- **Funds that don't lead.** They join rounds but rarely set the terms.
- **Funds that have gone quiet.** No new lead in 12+ months, and the fund is near the end of its life.
- **Funds with a conflict.** They already backed a direct competitor, so pitching them means handing your deck to a rival's board member.

Investors have the mirror problem. At Slush they meet 30+ startups in two days and need to know fast whether a startup competes with their portfolio and who has backed its rivals.

content.text:
Yes. Each agent works on its own short-lived branch, one per task, and merges straight into `main` when the task's tests pass. No separate tool or lead agent runs the show. The agents coordinate through files in the repo, and the three of you sync up at the checkpoint (CP) times listed in `TODO.md`.

**The loop each agent follows** (from the rules in `CLAUDE.md`):
1. `git pull --rebase` on `main`.
2. Pick its next unchecked task in `TODO.md`, after checking that every task under `Needs:` is already ticked on `main`.
3. Create a branch, e.g. `b/B3-find-competitors`.
4. Write code only in its own folders, committing with titles like `[B3] …`.
5. When the tests pass, rebase onto the latest `main`, merge, push, and delete the branch.
6. Tick its task in `TODO.md` in a separate small commit and push.

**How the three agents stay in sync without talking to each other:**

| Mechanism | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `TODO.md` + `Needs:` | Sets the order. An agent only starts a task once the tasks it depends on are ticked on `main`. |
| `contracts/` (frozen after T2) | The fixed interface between A, B and C. Each can build against it with fake data without waiting for the others. |
| Folder ownership | Agents never edit the same files, so merges almost never conflict. |
| `notes/A.md` etc. | Requests for another area. The agent writes the request there, and its person passes it on to the owner. |
| Entire checkpoints | A record of why each change was made, which other agents can look up. |
| CP times | The three humans check that the pieces actually connect. |

**What the agents can't do** is notice another agent's work on their own. They only see it when they pull. So the people are the message bus: when A says "A2 is merged", B and C tell their agents to pull and continue. Each person works in their own clone, so separate worktrees only matter if one person runs two agents at once.

`CLAUDE.md` doesn't yet list the exact merge commands for step 5, so each agent may handle that step slightly differently. Should I add a short "task loop" section with the exact commands so all three agents do it the same way?

# Otium — hackathon repo (project: Pitchlist)

Several people, each with their own coding agent, work in this repo at once. `AGENTS.md` points to this
file, so every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) reads the same instructions.

**Read this whole file before writing any code.** A human will tell you which agent you are:
**Agent A (Data & infra)**, **Agent B (Intelligence)** or **Agent C (Product)**.
Your tasks are in `TODO.md` under your letter. Do them in order, one short branch per task.
The full product write-up is in `OVERVIEW.md`.

> Start prompt for humans:
> `Read CLAUDE.md and TODO.md. You are Agent A. Start with the first unchecked A-task.`

## Project

- **Theme:** Junction 2026 — Cala challenge "Make Unicorns Real": a product for founders/investors built on Cala's public data.
- **Idea:** Pitchlist — who's a fit, and who has a conflict, from either side of the table (details in §1).
- **Stack:** Python/FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, Cala, Gemini, MongoDB Atlas, Verda (details in §3).
- **Run:** set in task T1 — backend `uvicorn api.main:app --reload` from `backend/`; frontend `npm run dev` in `frontend/`. Update this line when T1 lands.

---

## Entire (session tracking)

This repo uses [Entire](https://docs.entire.io). Git hooks attach each agent session to a commit as a **checkpoint** (stored in git refs, synced to `origin` on push). That lets everyone see why code exists and what other agents already tried.

- **Set this up once per clone:** `entire enable --agent <claude-code|codex|cursor|...>`. Git hooks are not cloned, so `entire status` shows "Enabled" even when nothing is being recorded. Check that `.git/hooks/post-commit` exists. If it doesn't, commits won't create checkpoints.
- For exact commands and flags, run `entire agent-help`; don't guess.
- **Before starting work**, see what others did: `entire checkpoint list`, `entire recap`, and `entire search "<topic>"`.
- **Before changing code you didn't write**, run `entire why <file>:<line>` or `entire checkpoint explain <sha>`.
- Don't commit `.entire/{tmp,metadata,logs}`; they are already gitignored. Don't edit `.claude/settings.json` hooks by hand.

---

## Coordination rules

The goal is to avoid merge conflicts. They come from long-lived branches and from several people editing the same files.

1. **One branch per task, kept short.** Branch from fresh `main` (`git pull --rebase` first). Name it `<letter>/<task-id>-<slug>`, e.g. `a/A3-cala-client`. Merge back as soon as the task's tests pass (aim for under an hour), then delete the branch. Commit title starts with the task ID: `[A3] Cala client: retries + concurrency limit`. No PR review is needed unless you touch someone else's area. Never force-push `main`.
2. **Stay in your own directory.** Only edit files in the area you own (table below). If you need a change in someone else's area, don't make it: write the request in `notes/<your letter>.md` and tell your human.
3. **Change shared files in small, separate commits.** Dependency manifests (`backend/pyproject.toml`, `frontend/package.json`), `.env.example`, `TODO.md` ticks: minimal edit, own commit, push right away. Don't bundle with feature work.
4. **Contracts are frozen after task T2.** `contracts/` (schemas, API, fixtures format) changes only when all three humans agree. Then bump `CONTRACT_VERSION`, note it in `contracts/CHANGELOG.md`, and update §5 of this file **in the same commit**. Exception: Agent A writes fixture data into `contracts/fixtures/` (tasks A1, A2).
5. **Give each agent its own worktree.** If one person runs several agents, put each in its own git worktree (`git worktree add ../otium-<task> -b <branch>`). Never run two agents in the same folder.
6. **Commit small and often, with clear messages.** Each commit becomes an Entire checkpoint. Write one line saying what changed and why.
7. **Resolve conflicts using intent.** Run `entire why <file>:<line>` on both sides to see what each change was for, then keep both behaviours. Ask a human if the two can't both be kept.
8. **Ask a human before broad refactors**, renaming shared files, or reformatting the whole repo.
9. **Don't add a dependency** if a few lines of code would do. Never commit secrets; put them in `.env`, which must be gitignored. Only Agent A adds variable *names* to `.env.example`.
10. **Keep sources attached and use IDs.** Every fact you pass on keeps its `sources: list[Source]`. Use Cala entity IDs, never names, as keys (Cala has 5 different "Inventure"s).
11. **If a task is unclear or blocked, stop and ask your human.** Don't guess across someone else's area.

### Definition of done (every task)

- Code only in your area; contracts untouched.
- Tests for the new code pass (`pytest backend/tests/<your folder>` or `npm run build && npm test` in `frontend/`); `ruff` / `eslint` clean.
- Returns or serves contract models; sources preserved.
- Task ticked in `TODO.md` (your own line only) in a separate small commit.

---

11. **If a task is unclear or blocked, stop and ask your human.** Don't guess across someone else's area.

### Task loop (every task, exactly like this)

```sh
# 1. Start: fresh main, then pick the task
git switch main && git pull --rebase
git fetch origin 'refs/entire/*:refs/entire/*'      # teammates' checkpoints
#    Next task = your first unchecked task in TODO.md whose `Needs:` are all [x] on main
#    and whose gate (table below) is open. If none is ready, tell your human what you're waiting for.
git switch -c b/B3-find-competitors                 # <letter>/<task-id>-<slug>

# 2. Work: only in your folders, small commits titled "[B3] ..."

# 3. Finish: once the definition of done (below) is met
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main          # rerun your tests if anything new came in
git switch main && git pull --rebase
git merge --ff-only b/B3-find-competitors           # if it fails, main moved: go back to the branch and repeat step 3
git push origin main && git branch -d b/B3-find-competitors

# 4. Tick: your own TODO.md line only, in its own commit
git add TODO.md && git commit -m "[B3] done" && git push origin main
```

If a push is rejected: `git pull --rebase`, rerun your tests, push again. Never `--force`.

A gate is open when its task is ticked on `main`. To check: `git pull --rebase && grep -E '^- \[x\] \*\*A2 ' TODO.md` (replace A2 with the task that opens the gate).

content.text:
Both are added to `CLAUDE.md` and pushed to `main`. Your own `CLAUDE.local.md` now says `You are Agent B (Intelligence).` It's gitignored, so it stays on your machine.

**How roles work now:** each person runs one line in their clone, once:
```sh
echo "You are Agent A (Data & infra)." > CLAUDE.local.md
```
They then start every session with:
```
Read CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and TODO.md, then continue with my next task.
```
`CLAUDE.md` tells agents to read that file and to ask for a role if it's missing. So this also works for Codex or Cursor, which don't load `CLAUDE.local.md` on their own.

**Task loop:** `CLAUDE.md` now has the exact git commands for each task: start from a fresh `main`, branch, rebase, merge with `--ff-only`, push, delete the branch, and tick the task in its own commit. It never force-pushes. If the merge fails because `main` moved, the agent rebases again and retries.

**When the others can continue after A:** a gate counts as open once its task is ticked in `TODO.md` on `main`. Agents check that with a one-line `grep`.

| Gate | Opens when | What B and C can then do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **G0** | T1 + T2 (scaffold, contracts) done | You start B2 (Gemini wrapper); C starts C1 and C4 |
| **G1** (the main one) | **A2** done: fixtures plus a fake data store | All of B's core work on fake data; C's mock API and screens |
| **G2** | **A12** done: real Cala data works | B9: rerun your core work on real data |
| **G3** | **B10** done (that's you): founder mode works end to end | C connects to the real API; A deploys |

Agents only see each other's work after pulling. When an agent finishes a gate task, it tells its person "Gate Gx is open; tell the others to pull", and that person tells the team.

For you as B: until G1 is open, do only B2. Make sure A works only on A1 and then A2 at first, because everyone else is waiting on those two tasks.


If `git pull` reports local changes, they can run `git stash` first and then pull again. Nobody should have changes yet, though.

Then each person starts a **new** agent session, so it loads the latest `CLAUDE.md`, and pastes the prompt for their letter from my previous message. Everything there still applies, including the first step that creates `CLAUDE.local.md`. Start them in this order:

1. **A first**, right away. It works on T1 and T2 while the rest of you pick the demo cases.
2. **B (you) and C** next. Until A's agent finishes T2, your agents only review the contracts and write no code, so there's no risk of conflicts.
3. When A's agent says it has merged T2, all three of you check `contracts/schemas.py` and say OK. A ticks T2, which opens G0, and B and C tell their agents: `G0 is open, pull and continue.`

"""Pitchlist contracts: data models and the data-layer interface.

FROZEN after task T2. Changes need all three humans to agree; then bump
CONTRACT_VERSION, note it in contracts/CHANGELOG.md and update CLAUDE.md §5
in the same commit.
"""

from typing import Literal, Protocol

from pydantic import BaseModel

CONTRACT_VERSION = "1.0.0"

SourceRank = Literal["PRIMARY", "FILING", "PRESS", "AGGREGATOR", "UNKNOWN"]


# --- 5.1 Models ---------------------------------------------------------------


class Source(BaseModel):
    name: str
    url: str | None = None
    date: str | None = None  # ISO date or partial ("2025-10")
    rank: SourceRank = "UNKNOWN"


class EntityRef(BaseModel):
    id: str  # Cala UUID
    name: str
    type: str  # Company | Organization | Person | FundingRound ...
    description: str | None = None


class Company(EntityRef):
    industries: list[str] = []
    stage: str | None = None
    country: str | None = None
    total_funding_text: str | None = None
    sources: list[Source] = []


class RoundInvestor(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    is_lead: bool | None = None  # None = unknown


class Round(BaseModel):
    id: str
    company_id: str
    label: str | None = None  # "Seed", "Series A" ...
    date: str | None = None
    amount_text: str | None = None
    amount_eur: float | None = None
    investors: list[RoundInvestor] = []
    sources: list[Source] = []


class PortfolioLink(BaseModel):
    investor_id: str
    company: EntityRef
    sources: list[Source] = []


class PersonLink(BaseModel):
    person: EntityRef
    company_id: str
    role: Literal["BOARD", "FOUNDER", "CEO", "EMPLOYEE"]
    sources: list[Source] = []


class Competitor(BaseModel):
    company: Company
    reason: str
    similarity: float | None = None


class Conflict(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["PORTFOLIO", "BOARD"]
    competitor: EntityRef
    via_person: EntityRef | None = None
    sources: list[Source] = []


class Reason(BaseModel):
    text: str
    sources: list[Source] = []


class InvestorScore(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    score: float
    conflict: Conflict | None = None
    leads_in_space: int = 0
    rounds_in_space: int = 0
    last_lead_date: str | None = None
    warm_paths: list[Reason] = []
    reasons: list[Reason] = []


class FounderReport(BaseModel):
    company: Company
    competitors: list[Competitor]
    pitch: list[InvestorScore]
    skip: list[InvestorScore]


class InvestorCheck(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    company: Company
    conflicts: list[Conflict]
    competitors: list[Competitor]
    rounds: list[Round]


class Brief(BaseModel):
    investor_id: str
    company_id: str
    markdown: str
    citations: list[Source]


class AgentEvent(BaseModel):  # streamed by /api/jobs/{id}/stream and /api/chat
    type: Literal["step", "brief", "error", "done"]
    message: str | None = None
    brief: Brief | None = None


# --- 5.2 Data layer interface — A implements, B consumes ----------------------
# B only ever calls `data.get_store()`: FakeDataStore when USE_FAKE_STORE=true,
# else the real store.


class DataStore(Protocol):
    async def resolve(self, name: str, kind: Literal["company", "investor"]) -> list[EntityRef]: ...
    async def company(self, id: str) -> Company: ...
    async def rounds(self, company_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
    async def investor_rounds(self, investor_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
    async def portfolio(self, investor_id: str) -> list[PortfolioLink]: ...

content.content:
13:- **Funds with a conflict.** They already backed a direct competitor, so pitching them means handing your deck to a rival's board member.
15:Investors have the mirror problem. At Slush they meet 30+ startups in two days and need to know fast whether a startup competes with their portfolio and who has backed its rivals.
27:| Question | Who should I pitch, and who should I skip? | Is this a fit, does it conflict with my portfolio, and who backed its rivals? |
43:5. **Score them** in code (see Scoring).
68:| Not used | Tiger Data, Verda GPU clusters, fine-tuning | No real need; forcing them in hurts focus (and Verda's "Fit" score) |
78:| `entity_retrieval` with relationship projections | The backbone. `INVESTED_IN` for portfolios and conflicts, `PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND` for rounds and `is_lead`, `IS_BOARD_MEMBER_OF` / `FOUNDED` / `WORKS_AT` for board-seat conflicts and warm paths |
80:| `knowledge_search` | Fills gaps the graph is thin on (who led, how recently). Its `explainability` claims plus their references are shown as citations as-is, not rewritten by the LLM |
83:**What this lets us show that web search can't:** conflicts several hops away (competitor → investor → partner → board seat), co-investor warm paths, and how reliable each claim is.
87:An investor's score is the sum of four signals, and a conflict overrides the score. All of it is plain code with readable reasons, and the weights are a first guess to tune on real data on Saturday.
91:| Conflict | Backed a direct competitor (founder mode) or holds one (investor mode); or its partner sits on a competitor's board | Hard flag → "Don't pitch" list, with the competitor and a source |
109:| `rank_investors` | company ID | Scored investor list plus the "don't pitch" list |
156:class PersonLink(BaseModel): person: EntityRef; company_id: str; role: Literal["BOARD","FOUNDER","CEO","EMPLOYEE"]; sources: list[Source]
158:class Conflict(BaseModel): kind: Literal["PORTFOLIO","BOARD"]; competitor: EntityRef; via_person: EntityRef | None; sources: list[Source]
160:class InvestorScore(BaseModel): investor: EntityRef; score: float; conflict: Conflict | None; leads_in_space: int; rounds_in_space: int; last_lead_date: str | None; warm_paths: list[Reason]; reasons: list[Reason]
161:class FounderReport(BaseModel): company: Company; competitors: list[Competitor]; pitch: list[InvestorScore]; skip: list[InvestorScore]
163:class Brief(BaseModel): investor_id: str; company_id: str; markdown: str; citations: list[Source]
191:| POST | `/api/chat` | `{company_id?, investor_id?, message}` | Streamed text plus citations |

content.text: The SDK supports `response_json_schema`. Next I'll check what it actually sends for a nested Pydantic model, capturing the request without calling the network.

input.command:
. .venv/bin/activate && python - <<'EOF' 2>&1 | tail -30
import asyncio, json
from google import genai
from google.genai import types
from contracts.schemas import Competitor
from pydantic import BaseModel
class Out(BaseModel):
    competitors: list[Competitor]
c = genai.Client(api_key="x")
seen = {}
async def fake(http_method, path, request_dict, http_options=None, **kw):
    seen["path"]=path; seen["body"]=request_dict
    raise RuntimeError("captured")
c._api_client.async_request = fake
for name, cfg in [("json_schema", dict(response_json_schema=Out.model_json_schema())), ("schema_cls", dict(response_schema=Out))]:
    try:
        asyncio.run(c.aio.models.generate_content(model="m", contents="hi", config=types.GenerateContentConfig(temperature=0, response_mime_type="application/json", system_instruction="sys", **cfg)))
    except Exception as e:
        print(name, type(e).__name__, str(e)[:100])
    b = seen.get("body", {})
    gc = b.get("generationConfig", {})
    print(name, seen.get("path"), sorted(gc), "systemInstruction" in b)
    print(json.dumps(gc)[:300])
EOF

"""Gemini wrapper (B2): one call that returns a validated Pydantic model.

Every Gemini call in core/ and agent/ goes through `structured()`. Model names come from
GEMINI_MODEL_FAST / GEMINI_MODEL_SMART, the key from GEMINI_API_KEY.
"""

import asyncio
import os
from functools import cache
from typing import Any, Literal, TypeVar

from google import genai
from google.genai import errors, types
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError

T = TypeVar("T", bound=BaseModel)

RETRY_CODES = {429, 500, 502, 503, 504}


class LLMError(RuntimeError):
    """Gemini is not configured, or no valid answer after all retries."""


def model_name(tier: Literal["fast", "smart"] = "fast") -> str:
    """Model id for a tier; `smart` falls back to the fast model when unset."""
    fast = os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL_FAST", "").strip()
    name = (os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL_SMART", "").strip() or fast) if tier == "smart" else fast
    if not name:
        raise LLMError("GEMINI_MODEL_FAST is not set in .env")
    return name


@cache
def _client() -> genai.Client:
    key = os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY", "").strip()
    if not key:
        raise LLMError("GEMINI_API_KEY is not set in .env")
    return genai.Client(api_key=REDACTED


async def structured(
    prompt: str,
    schema: type[T],
    *,
    system: str | None = None,
    tier: Literal["fast", "smart"] = "fast",
    retries: int = 3,
    backoff: float = 1.0,
    client: Any = None,
) -> T:
    """Ask Gemini for JSON matching `schema` (temperature 0) and return it validated.

    Retries on rate limits, 5xx, network errors and answers that don't validate.
    Raises LLMError when it still fails after `retries` attempts.
    """
    client = client or _client()
    config = types.GenerateContentConfig(
        temperature=0,
        system_instruction=system,
        response_mime_type="application/json",
        response_schema=schema,  # the SDK converts the Pydantic model to Gemini's schema format
    )
    last: Exception | None = None
    for attempt in range(retries):
        if attempt:
            await asyncio.sleep(backoff * 2 ** (attempt - 1))
        try:
            resp = await client.aio.models.generate_content(
                model=model_name(tier), contents=prompt, config=config
            )
            return schema.model_validate_json(resp.text or "")
        except errors.APIError as e:
            if e.code not in RETRY_CODES:
                raise LLMError(f"Gemini error {e.code}: {e.message}") from e
            last = e
        except (ValidationError, OSError) as e:  # bad/empty JSON, network trouble

"""agent/llm.py with a fake Gemini client: no key, no network."""

from types import SimpleNamespace

import httpx
import pytest
from google.genai import errors
from pydantic import BaseModel

from agent.llm import LLMError, model_name, structured


class Pick(BaseModel):
    ids: list[str]
    reason: str


class FakeGemini:
    """Stands in for genai.Client: returns (or raises) the queued replies in order."""

    def __init__(self, *replies):
        self.replies = list(replies)
        self.calls = []
        self.aio = SimpleNamespace(models=SimpleNamespace(generate_content=self._generate))

    async def _generate(self, *, model, contents, config):
        self.calls.append({"model": model, "contents": contents, "config": config})
        reply = self.replies.pop(0)
        if isinstance(reply, Exception):
            raise reply
        return SimpleNamespace(text=reply)


def api_error(code):
    cls = errors.ClientError if code < 500 else errors.ServerError
    return cls(code, {"error": {"code": code, "message": "boom", "status": "X"}})


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def env(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("GEMINI_MODEL_FAST", "flash-model")
    monkeypatch.delenv("GEMINI_MODEL_SMART", raising=False)


async def test_returns_validated_model_with_temperature_0_and_schema():
    fake = FakeGemini('{"ids": ["a", "b"], "reason": "same market"}')
    out = await structured("pick", Pick, system="be strict", client=fake)
    assert out == Pick(ids=["a", "b"], reason="same market")
    call = fake.calls[0]
    assert call["model"] == "flash-model"
    assert call["config"].temperature == 0
    assert call["config"].response_mime_type == "application/json"
    assert call["config"].response_schema is Pick
    assert call["config"].system_instruction == "be strict"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "first", [api_error(429), api_error(503), httpx.ConnectError("down"), "not json", None]
)
async def test_retries_transient_failures_then_succeeds(first):
    fake = FakeGemini(first, '{"ids": [], "reason": "ok"}')
    out = await structured("pick", Pick, backoff=0, client=fake)
    assert out.reason == "ok" and len(fake.calls) == 2


async def test_gives_up_after_retries():
    fake = FakeGemini(api_error(503), api_error(503), api_error(503))
    with pytest.raises(LLMError, match="after 3 attempts"):
        await structured("pick", Pick, backoff=0, client=fake)
    assert len(fake.calls) == 3


async def test_client_errors_are_not_retried():
    fake = FakeGemini(api_error(400))
    with pytest.raises(LLMError, match="400"):
        await structured("pick", Pick, backoff=0, client=fake)
    assert len(fake.calls) == 1


def test_model_names_from_env(monkeypatch):
    assert model_name("smart") == "flash-model"  # smart falls back to fast
    monkeypatch.setenv("GEMINI_MODEL_SMART", "pro-model")
    assert model_name("smart") == "pro-model"
    monkeypatch.setenv("GEMINI_MODEL_FAST", "")
    with pytest.raises(LLMError, match="GEMINI_MODEL_FAST"):
        model_name()

B2 is done and on `main`. It's ticked in `TODO.md`, and all 16 backend tests pass.

**What it does** (`backend/agent/llm.py`): `structured(prompt, Model)` sends a prompt to Gemini and returns its answer as a checked Pydantic model.
- It sets temperature to 0 and reads the model names from `.env`.
- It retries rate limits, Gemini server errors, network errors and answers that aren't valid JSON or don't fit the model. It gives up after 3 attempts.
- Other errors fail straight away with a clear message.

It uses Google's official `google-genai` SDK. I added it to `backend/pyproject.toml` in its own commit, so **teammates need to re-run `pip install -e "backend[dev]"`** after pulling.

I used the SDK instead of calling Gemini's web API directly because Google's docs have moved to a newer API, and I couldn't confirm the raw request format. I did check, without a network call, that the SDK sends a JSON schema request that includes the nested contract models.

It hasn't been tested against real Gemini yet because there's no key. That's noted in `notes/B.md` and is one call to check once the key arrives.

**Entire isn't recording.** No commit since the very first one has a checkpoint, including A's T1 and T2 commits.
- **This session:** it started before the repo had any commits, so Entire couldn't set it up. Starting a new session for your next task fixes it from then on. If you also want tonight's work saved, I can attach this session to the latest commit. That uploads this conversation as a new checkpoint straight to GitHub.
- **A's commits:** A's agent probably isn't hooked up. A should check that `.git/hooks/post-commit` exists in their clone and, if it doesn't, run `entire enable --agent <agent>`. C should check the same.
